spec_match.rationale: Live WGSL compilation via createShaderModule()+getCompilationInfo() with enable subgroups/subgroup_uniformity toggles is the right demonstration, but the subgroup_uniformity chip is driven by the adapter's 'subgroups' GPU feature rather than navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures.has('subgroup_uniformity') (the spec's advertised surface and what the conformance suite checks), and an unused check for device.features.has('subgroup-uniformity') references a non-existent feature name.

interactive.rationale: Preset select, editable WGSL textarea, enable-directive checkboxes, and a Compile button that degrades to a clear 'WebGPU device not available. Cannot compile.' message without a device (CDP-verified click).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises live compilation with driver messages and toggling the feature to see acceptance change; the page implements exactly that (observable only on subgroups-capable GPUs).

edge_cases.rationale: Distinct branches for no-WebGPU, no-adapter (honest flag/GPU banner, verified rendering here), adapter-without-subgroups, and compile-time driver messages.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5673998232977408, the WGSL spec, and all three siblings.

conformance.rationale: The targeted feature suite (wgslLanguageFeatures + subgroup_uniformity + adapter subgroups) matches this page's intent and honestly fails its three GPU-dependent assertions in this environment.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Adapter-unavailable banner, chip states, editor, and the no-device compile path verified via CDP with clean console; real driver compilation output requires a subgroups-capable GPU absent here.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Editor, chips, and buttons use shared variables; compile button follows the global button contract.

accessibility.rationale: The WGSL textarea has an aria-label and toggles are real checkboxes, but compile status/messages and feature chips update without live regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured at 360px: the preset label+select row reaches 409px and the select is partially clipped by body overflow-x:hidden — a control is cut on narrow phones.

openQuestions.title: Drive the subgroup_uniformity chip from wgslLanguageFeatures
openQuestions.detail: The chip labelled 'subgroup_uniformity (Chrome 145+)' is set from adapter.features.has('subgroups'), which can be true on browsers that lack the language feature (and vice versa); probe navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures.has('subgroup_uniformity') — the surface the spec and the conformance suite define — and delete the dead device.features.has('subgroup-uniformity') check.

openQuestions.title: Fix clipped preset select on mobile
openQuestions.detail: At 360px the preset row measures 409px and the <select> is partially cut. Let the label wrap or give the row flex-wrap so the control stays fully tappable.

summary: Well-built playground with genuinely graceful degradation — the no-adapter banner, feature chips, and the guarded compile path all verified here — but its headline capability chip probes the wrong surface (adapter feature instead of wgslLanguageFeatures) and the preset select clips at 360px. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
